questions.question: What is Microsoft Entra ID?

options.text: Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service
An on-premises domain controller you must install
options.why: Entra ID is a cloud service.

questions.explanation: Entra ID provides authentication, SSO, MFA, application management and more.

questions.scenario: A legacy application in Azure requires domain join, Group Policy and Kerberos authentication, but the company does not want to deploy or manage domain controllers.
questions.question: Which service should it use?

options.why: Correct. It provides managed domain services.
DNS alone does not provide domain join or Kerberos.

questions.explanation: Entra Domain Services offers domain join, Group Policy, LDAP and Kerberos/NTLM as a managed service.

questions.question: Which authentication method requires two or more forms of verification, such as a password and a code from a phone app?

options.why: SSO lets one sign-in access many apps.

questions.explanation: MFA combines something you know, something you have, and/or something you are.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of single sign-on (SSO)?

options.text: Users sign in once with one identity to access many applications
Users never need a password or any credential
It replaces the need for permissions

questions.explanation: SSO reduces the number of credentials users manage and simplifies access management.

questions.question: Which TWO are passwordless authentication methods supported with Microsoft Entra ID?

options.text: Sharing a password with a colleague

questions.explanation: Passwordless options include Windows Hello for Business, Microsoft Authenticator and FIDO2 security keys/passkeys.

questions.scenario: A company wants to let consultants from a partner organisation sign in with their own work accounts to access a specific internal app.
questions.question: Which capability should it use?

options.why: Correct. Guests use their own credentials.

options.text: Create new local passwords for each consultant on a VM

questions.explanation: External identities let partners, vendors and customers use their own identities to access your apps.

questions.scenario: Users signing in from inside the corporate network should be allowed in normally, but sign-ins from unknown locations must require MFA.
questions.question: Which feature should you use?

options.why: Correct. It evaluates signals such as location to make access decisions.
RBAC controls permissions on resources, not sign-in conditions.

questions.explanation: Conditional Access uses signals (user, location, device, app, risk) to allow, require MFA or block.

questions.question: In Azure RBAC, a role assignment applied at a resource group scope affects what?

options.text: The resource group and all resources within it
options.why: Correct. Permissions are inherited by child scopes.

options.text: Only the resource group object, not the resources

questions.explanation: RBAC assignments at a scope are inherited by everything below it.

questions.scenario: An auditor must be able to view all resources in a subscription but must not change anything.
questions.question: Which built-in role should be assigned?

options.why: Contributor can create and modify resources.
Owner has full control, including access management.

questions.explanation: Assign the least privilege needed. Reader gives read-only access.

questions.question: Which TWO are guiding principles of the Zero Trust model?

options.text: Trust everything inside the corporate network
options.why: This is the old perimeter model that Zero Trust replaces.

options.text: Give everyone administrator rights to reduce helpdesk calls

questions.explanation: Zero Trust principles are verify explicitly, use least privilege access, and assume breach.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the defense-in-depth model?

options.text: To use multiple layers of security so that if one layer is breached, others still protect the data
To rely on a single strong firewall
To store data in the deepest storage tier
To replace identity security with physical security

questions.explanation: Layers include physical, identity and access, perimeter, network, compute, application and data.

questions.question: In the defense-in-depth model, which layer is at the centre, the asset that all other layers ultimately protect?

options.why: Physical security is the outermost layer.
Network sits between perimeter and compute.

questions.explanation: The layers wrap around data, the most valuable asset.

questions.scenario: A company runs workloads in Azure, on-premises and in another public cloud. It wants one service to assess security posture and detect threats across all of them.
questions.question: Which service should it use?

options.why: Correct. It covers Azure, hybrid and multi-cloud.
Policy enforces rules but does not detect threats.

questions.explanation: Defender for Cloud provides posture management and workload protection across environments.

questions.question: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?

options.text: Authentication proves who you are; authorization decides what you can do
Authentication decides what you can do; authorization proves who you are

questions.explanation: AuthN = identity (who). AuthZ = permissions (what). Entra ID handles authentication; RBAC handles Azure authorization.
